searchText: So we have our beefy machine for CI! I have akula set up on it. I'm looking into options for what CI/build server to use. I've personally used [Jenkins] and [Buildbot] before, and they're both fine. I'm also looking into [Woodpecker]. So far I'm leaning towards Woodpecker, but since it uses Docker, I'm concerned about build processes having root permissions. [Jenkins]: https://www.jenkins.io/ [Buildbot]: https://buildbot.net/ [Woodpecker]: https://woodpecker-ci.org/ Github also allows you to add your own runners to a repository or organization. So you could use github actions with your build server and stay within the github ecosystem (if that's preferred of course). Oh that's an interesting idea. Do you know if builds can access state on the runner? Yup, they can 😄 So you can pin a version of a package on a machine and all the CI runs would automatically use that version. Or perhaps give access to a sync'd archive node on the same machine? Yea, you can do API calls to the archive node if that's the aim here Direct disk access actually :\ We open akula's state db directly ooo, I'm not sure about that one tbh. I know that github uses some concept of workspaces, I guess if the data is in the workspace you can read it? Can't say i've tried this in the past... It's a bit weird for sure.

So we have our beefy machine for CI! I have akula set up on it.

I'm looking into options for what CI/build server to use.

I've personally used [Jenkins] and [Buildbot] before, and they're both fine.

I'm also looking into [Woodpecker].

So far I'm leaning towards Woodpecker, but since it uses Docker, I'm concerned about build processes having root permissions.

[Jenkins]: https://www.jenkins.io/
[Buildbot]: https://buildbot.net/
[Woodpecker]: https://woodpecker-ci.org/
